newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVENERGO PRIVATISED BY NOV - PM SHKELE.
newsitem.headline: LATVENERGO PRIVATISED BY NOV - PM SHKELE.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele said on Thursday that the country's largest energy producer Latvenergo would be trading on the stock exchange in November.
"I think the shares will be in the market by November," Shkele told Reuters in an interview on Thursday.
He said the process had taken longer than expected.
"Unfortunately, things are not developing so quicklky presently," he said.
Shkele said the government was well prepared for the remaining privatisations.
He believed the government would reach its target to complete the privatisation plan before the middle of next year.
"All this has been prepared now and with this we have showed that private property is safe now," he added.
The privatisation of the oil terminal Ventspils Nafta will proceed.
"With Ventspils Nafta we will be going straight ahead with the privatisation," said Shkele.
As regards the Latvian Gas company, Shkele believes it will also be privatised before the end of 1997, and that the government will hold less than 50 percent.
